title: Kanya puja: girls as the Goddess
hookLine: a pot of earth with seeds, a fast, and on the eighth day small girls seated and fed as the Goddess
carry: kanya puja: every girl honored as the goddess
tomorrow: Janmashtami: the universe in a baby's mouth
last: NAVARATRI: THE SAME POWER, NINE FACES.

lines: A POT, MANGO LEAVES, A COCONUT.
cards: It's the first morning of Navaratri in an apartment in Delhi. Before breakfast, someone spreads a layer of soil in a shallow tray and scatters barley over it.
In the middle goes a clay pot of water, mango leaves tucked around its neck, a coconut on top. A lamp is lit beside it. Then everyone leaves for work and school.
There's nothing to see yet, just a pot and some dirt. But by the ninth day, that tray will be a small field of green.

teach.b: Start at the end of the Goddess's book. The last demon king has fallen, and the gods, saved, sing her one more hymn of thanks.

teach.h: EVERY WOMAN IS A FORM OF YOU.
teach.b: In it they say something families still act out: every kind of knowledge is a form of you, Goddess, and so is every woman in the world. And she answers with a promise: whenever trouble rises, call me, and I'll come again.
It opens with ghatasthapana. Ghata, the pot. Sthapana, setting it up.

Many families invite the Goddess to be present in that pot for the nine days, and sow barley beside it, jau in Hindi. Many fast, some until evening, many by setting grain aside for buckwheat, fruit and milk.
Then, on the eighth or ninth day, comes the custom that surprises people most. Families invite young girls from the neighborhood into the house.
They wash the girls' feet, mark their foreheads, seat them like honored guests and feed them, often puri, chickpeas and a sweet halwa, with a small gift at the end.

teach.h: KANYA PUJA: GIRLS AS THE GODDESS.
teach.b: It's called kanya puja, and the girls are honored as forms of the Goddess herself. That's the teaching, said plainly. The Goddess isn't only in the pot or on the shrine.
Her power is honored in living girls and women, the ones at your own table. Many teachers draw the harder lesson too: a girl worshiped on the eighth night can't be treated as less on any other day.
On the tenth day comes Vijayadashami, the victory, and in some homes the green shoots are handed out as a blessing.

how: Many Hindus open Navaratri by setting up a pot as the Goddess's seat and sowing barley beside it, fast on some or all of the nine days, honor young girls as the Goddess in kanya puja on the eighth or ninth day, and keep the nights with garba in Gujarat, Durga Puja in Bengal and golu dolls in the South, ending on Vijayadashami.

s: a Navaratri fast always means eating nothing
many set grain aside and eat buckwheat, fruit and milk; some fast only until evening.
in kanya puja, young girls are honored as forms of the Goddess
on the eighth or ninth day their feet are washed, they're fed, and they're given a small gift.
in the gods' last hymn, every woman in the world is called a form of the Goddess
that's why girls can be seated and fed as the Goddess in kanya puja.

games.q: it's the eighth day, and girls from the neighborhood have arrived at your door for kanya puja. what comes first?
o: hand them sweets at the door and say goodbye.
wash their feet and seat them as honored guests.
ask them to sing for the family.
games.why: many families wash the girls' feet, mark their foreheads, seat them and feed them. for that hour, the guests at the table are honored as the Goddess.

practice: Picture the eighth morning: small girls in bright clothes on a mat, a brass plate, a pitcher of warm water. If you pray, pour the water over a small pair of feet in your mind, and say Jai Mata Di.
If you don't, think of one girl or woman whose strength goes unthanked, a sister, a teacher, a grandmother, and choose one real way to honor her this week.

wordCard.voice: Navaratri. Nine nights of the Goddess, kept with a pot and seeds, a fast, girls honored as her forms, and the tenth day's victory.

orig.note: Sanskrit: nava, nine, and ratri, night. many say navratri in Hindi and Gujarati.

carryVoice: Your line: kanya puja. Every girl honored as the Goddess. Day one hundred forty-four, done.
